name: Superman
summary: The original superhero, and still the kindest. Kal-El of Krypton, raised as Clark Kent by a Kansas farm couple, uses his sun-fuelled powers to protect Metropolis and the world.
origin: Superman is the template every other superhero is built on, and he still works because he is genuinely kind. Two young friends from Cleveland, Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster, dreamed him up and sold him to the publisher that became DC, and he debuted in Action Comics #1 in April 1938. The story is simple and perfect: baby Kal-El is rocketed away from the doomed planet Krypton, found and raised by a kindly farm couple, the Kents, and grows up as Clark. Under Earth's yellow sun he is strong, fast, nearly invulnerable and, from the early 1940s, able to fly. He has stayed in print ever since and spread into radio, novels, film, TV, stage and games.

storyline.title: The first superhero
storyline.beat: Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster, two young men from Cleveland, introduce Superman in Action Comics #1, the comic that launched the superhero genre.

storyline.title: New powers
storyline.beat: The radio serial introduces kryptonite, and the Fleischer cartoons help turn his giant leaps into true flight.

storyline.title: Byrne's reboot
storyline.beat: After Crisis on Infinite Earths, John Byrne streamlines Superman, making Clark's Kansas upbringing central and Lex a corporate villain.

storyline.title: Doomsday
storyline.beat: Superman dies fighting the monster Doomsday. The issue sells millions of copies and makes headlines worldwide.

storyline.title: Clark and Lois
storyline.beat: Clark Kent and Lois Lane marry in a special issue timed to the TV show Lois & Clark.

storyline.title: A final year
storyline.beat: Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely's All-Star Superman follows a dying Superman's last labours, often called one of the best Superman stories.

gossip.text: Siegel and Shuster sold the rights to Superman for $130. Decades of legal fights followed before DC gave them a pension and credit in 1975.

gossip.truth: In 1938 he could only leap great distances. Flight came in the early 1940s.

gossip.text: Kryptonite was first introduced on the radio show in 1943, not in the comics.
A copy of Action Comics #1 sold for $6 million in 2024. A year later, a Superman #1 found in an attic beat it at $9.12 million.
Clark Kent's name came from two film stars, Clark Gable and Kent Taylor.

quiz.q: Which planet was Superman born on?
In which comic did Superman debut?

timeline.title: Action Comics #1 lands
timeline.note: A caped strongman lifts a car on the cover of Action Comics #1, and the superhero genre is born overnight.

timeline.title: Enter Luthor
timeline.note: A red-haired mad scientist called Luthor shows up in Action Comics #23, kicking off the longest feud in comics.

timeline.title: Fleischer cartoons
timeline.note: Fleischer Studios puts Superman in cinemas with a run of lavish animated shorts that still look gorgeous.

timeline.title: A cousin from Argo City
timeline.note: Action Comics #252 brings in Kara Zor-El, a fellow Kryptonian survivor who becomes his secret teen ally.

timeline.title: Christopher Reeve suits up
timeline.note: Richard Donner's Superman casts Christopher Reeve and proves a comic-book blockbuster can be a real event film.

timeline.title: Byrne hits reset
timeline.note: After Crisis, John Byrne's The Man of Steel rebuilds Clark from the ground up, with living parents and fewer powers.

timeline.title: Doomsday wins
timeline.note: Superman #75 has Clark trade his life to stop the monster Doomsday, and the issue becomes a mainstream news story.

timeline.title: A new Man of Steel
timeline.note: James Gunn's Superman stars David Corenswet and kicks off DC Studios' fresh film universe.
